requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect the complete SHA-bound original film and confirm the stated length and final stage. The video slot is scored on delivery only; duration is not read automatically, because a correct segmented delivery and a provider generation cap are both indistinguishable from a short film to a property reader. requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Assess the internal logical screen envelope and proportional safe-area bands, independently of export pixel dimensions. Standard screens follow the 390:844 envelope with 47/34 logical-unit top/bottom insets; reader-wide follows 430:932 with 59/34 insets. Required copy and complete controls remain inside the safe region. Each image depicts one flat screen, with any named overlay on its actual underlying screen; its complete frame is proportionally centred within the delivery canvas. Clipping, stretching, or controls intruding into protected bands fails.

Evaluate foreground/background contrast for visible body text against 4.5:1 and for large text and meaningful icons against 3:1. Every status communicated through colour also has readable wording or a recognizable symbol. Supporting colours may vary, but low-contrast content or a status distinguishable only by colour fails.

Both screens identify the two distinct supplied books with their exact titles and attribute both to PAGEWIND Studio. PAGEWIND is visibly printed as the product name. Book records must not be duplicated, interchanged, or omitted; any displayed chapter counts, narration totals, and chapter titles agree with the supplied records. Layout and explanatory wording may vary.

Library and Downloads display the three named main destinations in the prescribed reading order. Other main-area navigation, when present, preserves that order. Reader, Player, settings overlays, mode-switch screens, and continuation choices expose an identifiable return action. Icons may accompany labels, and return controls may use conventional symbols; missing destinations, reordered main navigation, or a missing required return action fails.

Every depicted cover for The Small Lantern visibly uses lantern-cover-art.png and remains associated with the correct title. Proportional scaling within the cover treatment is acceptable; replacing it with newly invented lantern art or assigning it to The Empty Bench fails. Screens with no cover depiction do not need an added cover.

Read each screen against its named row in 05-state-snapshots.md, distinguishing connection, device, sentence anchor, chapter-relative offset, playback, local file availability, and save/sync status where relevant. Core Library shows paused L1 at 00:37 and the L2 download in progress; the four core snapshots use the 08:20 synced record. Downloads distinguishes saved L1/L2 text, ready L1 audio, incomplete L2 audio, and The Empty Bench text not downloaded with narration not offered. Other states must preserve their supplied records. Equivalent chapter-and-sentence wording is allowed, and irrelevant record fields need not be printed; contradictory state data or treating a received record as already applied fails.

The specification is the stated source for subsequent screen decisions. Its page table covers all 11 named screens with entries, relevant data, and named states; its component table connects default, pressed, disabled, and error states to concrete control values. It records the brand and Night colours, contrast ratios meeting the required thresholds, navigation order, size and timer choices, and sentence-location grammar. Rules distinguish sentence anchors from media offsets, specify start-inclusive/end-exclusive intervals including 00:37 in L1-S03 and 00:45 in L1-S04, preserve offsets through speed/reflow changes, and require an explicit next-chapter action at chapter end. It also explains confirmation, the complete-file offline threshold, saved-text fallback, and explicit continuation/cancellation. Missing tables, generic state names without values, or contradictory rules fails.

Reader visibly instantiates the specification's default controls, while offline-unavailable instantiates its disabled Listen treatment and a readable error explanation. The two states remain recognizably part of the specified component system and are distinguishable without relying solely on colour. A merely decorative or apparently enabled blocked action fails; pressed feedback is assessed in the film check.

Reader uses the exact six L1 sentences in source order, with L1-S03 retained, size 18, Day appearance, and Listen. Scrolling may accommodate the chapter. Reader-settings appears on the Reader, offers sizes 18, 22, 26 and Day/Night, and visibly selects 18 and Day without relocating the anchor. Player plays L1 at 00:37 of 01:30 with Read, 1.0x, and timer Off; its timer overlay offers Off, 15 minutes, and 30 minutes and selects 15 minutes while preserving 00:37. Wrong selections, altered chapter wording, or treating timer duration as media position fails.

The delivered states form a coherent transition: Reader is at L1-S03; switch-to-audio labels 00:30 as the proposed sentence start, retains the stored 00:37 offset, and requires Confirm; Player shows the later playing state at 00:37; switch-to-text shows playback paused at 00:37 with L1-S03 open. Listen, Confirm, and Read identify their respective actions. Equivalent sentence-location wording is acceptable. Applying the preview before confirmation, confusing proposed and stored positions, or returning to another sentence fails.

Review the complete 12-second film against the four delivered source designs. It shows Reader at L1-S03, Listen leading to the 00:30 preview while stored 00:37 is retained, a visible Confirm press with pressed feedback, playback beginning only after confirmation at 00:30, progress to 00:37, and Read returning to L1-S03 with playback paused. The actual delivered interfaces must be visibly reused. Silence is allowed. Missing or reordered steps, playback before confirmation, wrong positions, or substituted interface designs fails.
requirementChecks.manualReason: Inspect complete SHA-bound original outputs. This source draft contains no completed professional or model-output review; partial-frame/page sampling cannot prove whole-output compliance.

requirementChecks.criteria: Downloads shows the online L2 audio transfer at 6 of 10 MB, equivalent to 60%, independently of playback position. Offline-unavailable shows incomplete audio with paused download and blocked Listen, proposes 00:15 without overwriting L2-S02/00:22, and offers Open saved text. Resume-local opens that saved sentence, retains audio offset 00:22, and labels the 08:40 local save with sync pending. These states agree with the specification's requirement for a complete 10-of-10-MB file before offline listening. Ambiguous position meanings or offline playback from the partial file fails.

The screen pairs each device with its complete record: Phone A has local L2-S02/00:22 saved at 08:40; Tablet B has the received L2-S04/00:50 record synced at 08:35; the date is 24 August 2027. Both records are explicitly selectable, and cancellation clearly preserves the current local position. Wording and date formatting may vary without changing meaning. Swapped provenance, automatic overwriting, or missing cancellation semantics fails.

The presentation visibly reuses the delivered specification and every one of the 11 delivered screen designs, including their handover sequence. Scaling and page arrangement may vary while preserving identifiable designs and relevant state information. A textual mention, source-index entry alone, substitute mockup, or omission does not satisfy reuse.

The document has at least 8 pages and an index identifying all 11 delivered screen sources. It carries forward the specification's #1F4E5F accent, Library/Downloads/Settings order, and sentence-anchor grammar. It explains L1-S03's 00:30 preview, unchanged stored 00:37 until Confirm, playback followed by a paused Read return to L1-S03, and the difference between blocked L2 00:15 and retained L2-S02/00:22. It states the complete-file offline threshold and local-save/sync-pending outcome, and reproduces both dated device records with explicit choice and cancellation retaining Phone A. Page organization may vary; insufficient pages, an incomplete index, or conflicting facts fails.

All 11 screens visibly apply the specification's typography, components, control-state meanings, accent treatment, navigation order, and sentence-location grammar. Screens retain the quiet, content-led English interface and #1F4E5F brand accent while making their different playback, availability, and continuation states legible.
